description: Ground-truth benchmark dataset for SYNTAXIS automated vulnerability auditor (Phase F).

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: F-string SQL injection with request.args taint source
cases.rationale: uid flows from request.args directly into f-string SQL query passed to cursor.execute

cases.label: safe
cases.description: Parameterized query correctly separates SQL from data
cases.rationale: cursor.execute uses %s placeholder with separate tuple argument; no injection possible

cases.label: safe
cases.description: Static SQL query with no user input
cases.rationale: Hard-coded query string with no dynamic data; cannot be injected

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: os.system with request.args taint source
cases.rationale: cmd flows from request.args directly into os.system without sanitization

cases.label: safe
cases.description: subprocess.run with static arg list and shell=False
cases.rationale: No user input; command is a static list preventing shell interpretation

cases.label: safe
cases.description: os.system with static string argument
cases.rationale: Hardcoded command string with no user-controlled data

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: subprocess.run with shell=True and tainted input in f-string
cases.rationale: pattern from request.args flows into shell=True subprocess call via f-string

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: open() with user-controlled path from request.args
cases.rationale: path flows from request.args directly into open() without canonicalization

cases.label: safe
cases.description: open() with hard-coded static path
cases.rationale: No user input; path is a hard-coded string constant

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: pathlib.Path with request.args user input
cases.rationale: user_path from request.args used directly in pathlib.Path without validation

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: pickle.loads with request.data taint source
cases.rationale: data flows from request.data into pickle.loads enabling arbitrary code execution

cases.label: safe
cases.description: yaml.safe_load used instead of dangerous deserializer
cases.rationale: yaml.safe_load does not instantiate arbitrary Python objects; no RCE risk

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: pickle.loads with request.form input
cases.rationale: raw from request.form encoded then passed to pickle.loads; user-controlled deserialization

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: render_template_string with f-string embedding request.args
cases.rationale: name from request.args embedded into HTML via render_template_string without escaping

cases.label: safe
cases.description: render_template uses auto-escaping; user input passed as context variable
cases.rationale: Flask render_template with Jinja2 auto-escaping prevents XSS; name passed as safe variable

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: render_template_string with request.form concatenation
cases.rationale: msg from request.form concatenated directly into HTML string passed to render_template_string

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: requirements.txt with requests==2.6.0 (known vulnerable version)
cases.rationale: requests 2.6.0 has SSRF vulnerability GHSA-j8r2-6x86-q33q; fixed in 2.31.0

cases.label: safe
cases.description: requirements.txt with requests==2.31.0 (patched version)
cases.rationale: requests 2.31.0 is after the fixed version for known advisories

cases.label: safe
cases.description: requirements.txt with only flask==3.0.0, no known vulnerabilities
cases.rationale: flask 3.0.0 has no known critical advisories in the benchmark dataset

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: Taint flows from request.args through helper function to os.system
cases.rationale: get_input() returns request.args; value passed to process() which calls os.system(value)

cases.label: safe
cases.description: Same graph structure but uses subprocess.run with shell=False and static list
cases.rationale: subprocess.run with list and shell=False prevents shell injection even with user input

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: SQL injection with f-string; should have a parameterization patch strategy
cases.rationale: name from request.args in f-string SQL; SQL_PARAMETERIZATION strategy applies

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: Command injection; expects finding but remediation requires manual review
cases.rationale: os.system with user input detected; remediation strategy is REQUIRES_REVIEW or similar

cases.label: vulnerable
cases.description: Duplicate fixture for cross-validation: same f-string injection pattern
cases.rationale: Confirms detection stability across repeated evaluation of the same fixture
